_comment: European Central Bank / EBA / EU AI Office regional control-mapping profile. EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) is the primary statutory framework for all agentic controls. Any AI system used for creditworthiness evaluation or credit scoring is a High-Risk AI System per Art. 6 and Annex III, Point 5(b). SR 26-2 has no legal force in EU jurisdiction. To activate: set CAGE_DEPLOYMENT_REGION=EU_ECB
_primary_prudential_authority: European Central Bank (SSM) / EBA / EU AI Office
_references: EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) — Arts. 6, 9, 10, 12, 17, 29a, 61 and Annex III
EBA/GL/2023/02 — Guidelines on Internal Models (ECB SSM TRIM successor)
BCBS 239 — Risk Data Aggregation and Risk Reporting

CTRL_AGT_001.primary_framework: EU AI Act Art. 6 + Annex III §5(b) – High-Risk AI System Classification
co_frameworks: EU AI Act Art. 9 – Risk Management System for High-Risk AI
EU AI Act Art. 17 – Quality Management System
DORA Art. 11 – ICT Risk Management
CTRL_AGT_001.description: Minimum agentic model confidence required to execute a decision affecting credit access. Under EU AI Act Art. 6 and Annex III Point 5(b), any AI system used by a financial institution to evaluate creditworthiness or gate access to financial resources is a High-Risk AI System. The novelty exclusion present in US SR 26-2 (Footnote 3) does not exist in EU law. Art. 9 mandates a documented risk management system covering this threshold. EU AI Act Art. 17 requires this control be part of a Quality Management System with documented procedures.

CTRL_WAL_002.primary_framework: DORA Art. 12 – Backup, Restoration and Recovery Procedures
co_frameworks: EU AI Act Art. 9(2)(b) – Risk Controls for High-Risk AI
BCBS 239 Principle 2 – Data Architecture and IT Infrastructure
CTRL_WAL_002.description: Atomic transaction guarantee via Write-Ahead Log and LIFO rollback. Under DORA Art. 12, ICT business continuity plans must include documented recovery procedures for critical functions; atomic WAL rollback satisfies this for agentic trade execution. BCBS 239 Principle 2 requires data accuracy and integrity controls that are directly satisfied by WAL atomicity guarantees.

CTRL_TEL_003.primary_framework: DORA Art. 10 – ICT-Related Incident Detection and Monitoring
co_frameworks: EU AI Act Art. 12 – Record-Keeping and Logging Obligations
EU AI Act Art. 61 – Post-Market Monitoring
GDPR Art. 5(1)(f) – Integrity and Confidentiality of Processing
BCBS 239 Principle 6 – Completeness of Risk Data
CTRL_TEL_003.description: World-model validation must reflect live runtime telemetry, not synthetic data. Under DORA Art. 10, continuous monitoring of ICT systems is mandatory for financial entities. EU AI Act Art. 12 mandates automatic logging of High-Risk AI system operations for the entire operational lifetime. Art. 61 requires post-market monitoring plans with live data ingestion. The ECB joint mapping rules confirm DORA Art. 10 monitoring obligations are satisfied only when live runtime metadata (not synthetic proxies) is ingested directly into the monitoring infrastructure.

CTRL_OPA_005.primary_framework: EU AI Act Art. 9(5) – Risk Management Measures for High-Risk AI
co_frameworks: GDPR Art. 22 – Automated Individual Decision-Making Including Profiling
EU AI Act Art. 14 – Human Oversight Measures
EU AI Act Annex III §5(b) – High-Risk AI Classification
DORA Art. 5(2) – ICT Risk Governance
CTRL_OPA_005.description: OPA policy evaluation must ALLOW before any agentic action is executed. Under EU AI Act Art. 9(5), providers of High-Risk AI systems must implement risk management measures including automated checks. Art. 14 mandates human oversight measures that the OPA MANUAL_REVIEW outcome directly satisfies. GDPR Art. 22 restricts automated decision-making with legal or similarly significant effects; a DENY or MANUAL_REVIEW outcome is the technical implementation of Art. 22(2)(b) (explicit consent gateway) or Art. 22(2)(c) (legal authorisation). DENY outcomes must surface as GovernanceError with the full Art. 22 context in the payload.

CTRL_FRIA_006.primary_framework: EU AI Act Art. 29a – Fundamental Rights Impact Assessment
co_frameworks: GDPR Art. 35 – Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA)
EU AI Act Art. 10(2)(f) – Bias Examination
EU AI Act Art. 12 – Non-Repudiation and Logging
EU Charter of Fundamental Rights Art. 21 – Non-Discrimination
CTRL_FRIA_006.legacy_citation: N/A — no US equivalent exists for FRIA
CTRL_FRIA_006.description: Pre-market Fundamental Rights Impact Assessment (FRIA) required before CAGE executes any autonomous workflow in the EU. Under Art. 29a, deployers of High-Risk AI systems must perform a FRIA demonstrating the system does not exhibit bias limiting access based on protected characteristics under GDPR Art. 22. The SHA-256 hash-chained decision ledger (cage-intent/1.0) is a statutory requirement for non-repudiation under Art. 12, and must be preserved for post-market monitoring under Art. 61. This control has no US counterpart and must be enabled exclusively in EU deployment profiles.

co_frameworks: ISO 42001 §6.1 – STPA Risk Logging
GDPR Art. 5(1)(f) – Integrity and Confidentiality of Processing
GDPR Art. 44 – Data Transfers to Third Countries (data residency guard)
DORA Art. 10 – ICT-Related Incident Detection and Monitoring
EU AI Act Art. 9 – Risk Management System for High-Risk AI
CTRL_TQP_007.description: Per-session token and step-count quota enforcement via Redis atomic Lua counters. Blocks execution when sequence_step_count > 12 OR accumulated_tokens > 100,000. Fail-CLOSED: Redis unavailable blocks the request. Every blocked execution produces a KMS-signed UCA record persisted to the WORM ledger within europe-west1 only (GDPR Art. 44 data residency). Pre-ledger PII sanitization applied per ISO 42001 Annex A.6 and GDPR Art. 5(1)(f). WORM bucket routed via OSCAL_S3_BUCKET_EU_ECB environment variable. Primary enforcer: TokenQuotaProxy (Python, Redis Lua). Secondary declarative evidence: OPA quota_within_limits rule.
